html:
Surasena was an ancient kingdom around Mathura on the Yamuna, in the region now called Braj. Buddhist texts count it among the sixteen Mahajanapadas of the 6th century BCE.

Its fame is religious more than political. Mathura and its villages are the land of Krishna's childhood in Hindu tradition, and the clans of the area, such as the Yadavas and Vrishnis, appear in the epics. Around 300 BCE the Greek envoy Megasthenes described a people he called the Sourasenoi, around Mathura, who honoured a god he took for Herakles; many read this as an early sign of Krishna worship. See Megasthenes at Pataliputra.

Surasena was swallowed by Magadha and later the Maurya Empire. Mathura went on to be a great centre of art under the Kushans.
